GeneDef.label: fly brain
GeneDef.description: Carriers run on a compact neural controller distilled from an insect connectome. They choose their own work and rest and cannot be given work priorities or a schedule.\n\nWhen doing one of the jobs they chose as most important, they work 10% faster.

GeneDef.label: compound eyes
GeneDef.description: Carriers have faceted eyes wired to fast motion-detecting circuits. They react to movement quickly, aim faster, and are twice as likely to spot a trap before stepping on it.

GeneDef.label: escape reflex
GeneDef.description: Carriers have a single giant nerve fiber running from the eyes to the legs, like the escape circuit of a fly. When something swings at them, they are already moving.\n\nWhen attacked in melee, carriers have a 35% chance to hop 3-6 tiles away before the blow lands (at most once per hour). They don't do this while deliberately brawling.

GeneDef.label: sugar drive
GeneDef.description: Carriers crave sugar. Eating berries, insect jelly, chocolate, agave, ambrosia or a fine or lavish meal gives them a mood boost. Carriers with a fly brain also favor cooking and growing when the colony runs low on sweet food.

GeneDef.label: swarm sense
GeneDef.description: Carriers are soothed and sharpened by others of their kind. They work 3% faster for each other swarm-sense carrier of their faction within 12 cells (up to 12%), feel good in company, and feel lonely when none are on the map.

GeneDef.label: flight muscles
GeneDef.description: Carriers have vestigial wings and spring-loaded leg muscles that let them hop great distances. Unlike longjump legs, this does not need hemogen.

GeneDef.label: darting gait
GeneDef.description: Carriers move in short, quick bursts like a fly on a tabletop. They move a little faster than normal.

GeneDef.label: hive learning
GeneDef.description: Carriers pick up skills by watching others of their kind. Learning speed grows with the size of the swarm: +10% for each other hive-learning carrier of the same faction on the map, up to +50%.\n\nAlone, carriers learn 10% slower than normal.
